Delegation Agreement
Clinical and Operational Addendum (Document ID RIVERBEND-ADDENDUM) | Amended and restated
effective January 1, 2026

title: Scope of delegation
text:
1. Scope of delegation
Riverbend Health Plan ('Riverbend') delegates prior authorization for medical services to Bellcourt Health
Administrators ('Bellcourt') for two insured products: (a) Riverbend Medicare Advantage HMO, serving members
in Arizona and Texas; and (b) Riverbend Marketplace Silver HMO, an ACA individual-market plan serving
members in Georgia. Pharmacy prior authorization is not delegated. Riverbend retains ultimate accountability to
CMS and state regulators and oversees Bellcourt through quarterly delegation audits.

title: Clinical criteria
text:
2. Clinical criteria
Bellcourt shall apply the Bellcourt medical policy library in effect on the date of service, except as set out below.

title: Medicare Advantage: Medicare coverage rules take precedence
text:
2.1 Medicare Advantage: Medicare coverage rules take precedence
For Medicare Advantage members, where a Medicare National Coverage Determination (NCD) or applicable
Local Coverage Determination (LCD) exists, its criteria must be applied and Bellcourt criteria may not be more
restrictive. For the following services, Riverbend has confirmed the Medicare criteria to apply:
Service Criteria to apply for MA members (simplified training summary)
Continuous glucose monitors Diabetes mellitus AND either (a) insulin treatment of any type or frequency, or (b)
documented problematic hypoglycemia. Applies to all dates of service under this
Agreement.
CPAP continued coverage As MP-118 (4 or more hours per night on at least 70% of nights in a consecutive 30-day
period within the first 90 days).
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy As MP-112.
Home health services As MP-116.

title: Marketplace product
text:
2.2 Marketplace product
Bellcourt medical policies apply without modification.

title: Decision timeframes
text:
3. Decision timeframes
Product Standard pre-service Expedited / urgent Basis
Medicare Advantage 7 calendar days 72 hours CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final
Rule (CMS-0057-F), effective January 2026
Marketplace (GA) 15 calendar days 72 hours State law and Agreement
Clocks start when Bellcourt receives the request through any channel, including fax, regardless of whether it has
been entered into Bellcourt's systems.

title: Adverse determinations
text:
4. Adverse determinations
- Only a licensed physician may issue a denial based on medical necessity. Nurses may approve but may not
deny.
- For Arizona members, effective July 1, 2026, a medical director licensed in Arizona must personally review and
sign every denial of a medical-necessity request.
- Every denial notice must state the specific reason, cite the criteria relied on, and describe appeal rights.
- For Texas members, where any automated or AI-assisted tool was used in reviewing the request, the notice
must disclose that use.

title: Automation and artificial intelligence
text:
5. Automation and artificial intelligence
Bellcourt shall give Riverbend 60 days' written notice before deploying any automated or AI-assisted tool in the
prior authorization workflow. No such tool may deny, delay, or modify a request on its own; a qualified human
must make every adverse decision. Bellcourt must be able to produce, on audit, the inputs and outputs of any
such tool for a given case.

title: Performance standards and remedies
text:

title: Term and renewal
text:
7. Term and renewal
The current term ends December 31, 2026. Either party may elect not to renew with 90 days' notice. Riverbend
may terminate for cause if a Corrective Action Plan is not satisfied within 120 days.

title: Interoperability
text:
8. Interoperability
Bellcourt shall support Riverbend's obligations under CMS-0057-F, including an electronic prior authorization API,
provider access to prior authorization status, and public metrics reporting, by the dates set in that rule (January
2027 for API requirements).

title: Purpose and scope
text:
1. Purpose and scope
This policy sets out the clinical criteria Bellcourt reviewers use to decide whether the service described in this
policy (Advanced Imaging: MRI of the Lumbar Spine) is medically necessary. It is applied to prior authorization
requests where the date of service falls within the effective period stated above. A client's plan document may
exclude this service or impose additional requirements; plan provisions are checked first.

title: Definitions
text:
2. Definitions
Medically necessary: services that are appropriate and consistent with the diagnosis, in accordance with generally
accepted standards of medical practice, and not primarily for the convenience of the member or provider.

title: Coverage criteria
text:
3. Coverage criteria
The service is considered medically necessary when the criteria below are met, read together using the AND / OR
connectors shown:
1 Presence of a red-flag condition (suspected cauda equina syndrome, suspected spinal infection, suspected
malignancy, progressive neurological deficit, or significant trauma); OR
2 Radicular pain or radiculopathy that has persisted despite at least 6 weeks of documented conservative
therapy (physical therapy, supervised exercise, NSAIDs or activity modification).

title: Not medically necessary / limitations
text:
4. Not medically necessary / limitations
- Uncomplicated low back pain without radiculopathy and without red flags.
- Imaging requested solely for reassurance or at patient request.

title: Documentation requirements
text:
5. Documentation requirements
Office notes documenting symptom duration, neurological exam, conservative therapy type and duration;
surgeon's note if requested for pre-surgical planning.
If required documentation is missing, the request must be pended and the provider contacted for information. It
must not be denied for lack of documentation until the information request has gone unanswered within the
regulatory timeframe.

title: Version history
text:
6. Version history
Version Effective Summary

v2 2026-01-01 Conservative-therapy duration reduced from 6 weeks to 4 weeks; pre-surgical
planning added as an indication. Approved by the Clinical Policy Committee

Who it applies to
Medicare Advantage organizations, state Medicaid and CHIP programs (fee-for-service and managed care), and

REG-03: ERISA, Self-Funded Plans and the Role of
a TPA
Training summary prepared for the Bellcourt case study. Simplified for learning purposes; not legal advice
and not a substitute for the source text.
Self-funded versus fully insured
In a fully insured plan the employer buys a policy and the insurer bears the claims risk. In a self-funded plan the
employer bears the risk, pays claims from its own funds, and usually hires a TPA to administer the plan. Most
self-funded employers also buy stop-loss insurance to cap catastrophic claims.
Pre-emption
ERISA generally pre-empts state insurance laws for self-funded plans. State mandates (for example, required
coverage of particular services) and state AI-in-UR laws therefore generally do not bind self-funded plans. The
plan document controls what is covered.
Claims procedure timeframes (29 CFR 2560.503-1)
- Urgent care claims: 72 hours.
- Pre-service claims: 15 days, with one 15-day extension if needed.
- Post-service claims: 30 days, with one 15-day extension.
Notice content
An adverse benefit determination must state the specific reason, reference the plan provision relied on, describe
any additional information needed and why, and explain the appeal procedure.
